question: A 45-year-old male is presenting for routine health maintenance. He has no complaints. His pulse if 75/min, blood pressure is 155/90 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 15/min. His body mass index is 25 kg/m2. The physical exam is within normal limits. He denies any shortness of breath, daytime sleepiness, headaches, sweating, or palpitations. He does not recall having an elevated blood pressure measurement before. Which of the following is the best next step?

paths: (Hypertensive disease)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(arterial stiffness)-PROCESS_OF->(Entire femoral artery)-LOCATION_OF->(Blood pressure determination)
(Hypertensive disease)-CAUSES->(arterial stiffness)-PROCESS_OF->(Entire femoral artery)-LOCATION_OF->(Blood pressure determination)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Elevated blood pressure reading" -> "Repeat the blood pressure measurement" -> 95% CHAIN: "Elevated blood pressure reading" -> "Check for white coat hypertension" -> "Repeat the blood pressure measurement" -> 90% CHAIN: "Elevated blood pressure reading" -> "Assess for lifestyle factors contributing to hypertension" -> "Repeat the blood pressure measurement" -> 95%
enhanced_information: For a 45-year-old male with an elevated blood pressure reading, the best next step is to repeat the blood pressure measurement to confirm the diagnosis. Lifestyle factors contributing to hypertension should also be assessed. There is no need for immediate referral to a cardiologist or initiation of treatment with a thiazide diuretic based on the current presentation.
analysis: The core medical principle in this scenario is to confirm the diagnosis of hypertension before initiating any treatment or referrals. Given the patient's lack of symptoms and no prior history of elevated blood pressure, the best next step is to repeat the blood pressure measurement to rule out white coat hypertension or other transient causes. Lifestyle modifications should also be discussed. Immediate referral to a cardiologist or starting medication is not warranted at this point.
